_README: Reference values for met/reconstruction.py estimators.
WHAT THIS FILE IS, AND IS NOT.  The Willoughby cases below are computed from
the published Eq. (7a) coefficients, so they check that the implemented
functional form matches the transcribed constants -- a TRANSCRIPTION check.
They are NOT independent verification: values derived from the coefficients
cannot validate the coefficients.  Nor can the physical invariants in
tests/test_reconstruction.py (monotonicity, positivity, SI magnitude), all of
which pass with a units error still in place.
The real verification is skill against observation:
test_skill_against_observed_rmw holds out the ~21,700 IBTrACS North Atlantic
1980-2025 points that DO report an RMW and checks median bias and MAE. A
units or wind-convention error fails that immediately.  It is marked remote
because it needs the archive; run it with GEOCLAW_TRACK_ARCHIVES set.
If a published table of (V_max, latitude) -> R_max values is located, add
those cases with 'source': 'paper, Table N' and set tolerance_m from the
paper's reported scatter.  That would upgrade this to real verification.
Eq. (7a) is fit to maximum azimuthally averaged FLIGHT-LEVEL winds
(predominantly 850/700 hPa), not to a storm file's 10 m point maximum; the
paper contrasts the two explicitly.  reconstruction.to_willoughby_wind does
the conversion.  max_wind_speed in the cases below is already on the
flight-level basis.

willoughby_2006_rmw.units: R_max km, V_max m/s, latitude degrees
willoughby_2006_rmw._tolerance_note: 1 m -- this is a transcription check against values computed from the same coefficients, so the tolerance is arithmetic, not physical.  A paper-sourced case would use the paper's reported scatter instead.
